home.intro: Build Victoria 3 mods from the data of your own game and mods. The game files and other mods are never changed: everything you make here is written to a separate new mod.
home.detect_failed: Could not find the folders automatically. Please choose them by hand.
home.mods_hint: Tick the mods whose content should be available in the builder. The order is the load order: when several sources define the same thing, the later mod wins, and mods always win over the base game.
home.load_hint: Reads companies, buildings, modifiers, states and names from the game and the selected mods.
home.stale: The folders or the mod selection changed since the data was loaded. Reload to use the new selection.
home.project_hint: Everything you build is saved into a mod of its own in the local mod folder. You can come back and keep editing it later.
home.project_none: No mod chosen yet. Create one or open an existing one.
home.need_project: Create or open your mod first.
home.types: What do you want to build?
home.type.company_hint: Add new companies or change existing ones.
map.failed: The map could not be loaded.
company.need_data: The game data is not loaded yet.
version_note.active: This is the version in effect in the game. Override and copy use the selected version.
version_note.same: This version has the same content as the one in effect.
version_note.hidden: This version differs from the one in effect in its conditions, AI or other script (not shown here).
version_note.shown: This version differs from the one in effect.
sidebar.title: Mod contents
editor.close: Close and go back to the start screen
editor.start_hint: Start a new one here, open one of your mod's items on the left, or pick an existing one on the right to change or copy.
company.discard_confirm: The company you are editing has unsaved changes. Discard them?
company.already_in_project: Your mod already changes this company. Opened that version.
company.override_note: This changes an existing company from: {source}. The original files are not touched; your mod replaces the whole definition when it is loaded after them.
company.key_hint: Internal name used in the files. Use letters, digits and _, usually starting with company_.
company.name: Name ({language})
company.name_hint: Switch the language in the top right corner to enter the name in other languages. Languages left empty are not written.
company.name_hint_override: Leave empty to keep the original name. Switch the language in the top right corner for other languages.
company.category_hint: Which kind of owner runs the company.
company.flavored_hint: Flavored companies are tied to specific countries or regions; generic ones are available to everyone.
company.images_hint: Pick from the pictures of the game and the loaded mods, or import your own (packed into the mod when you save).
company.building_types_hint: Buildings the company can own and boost.
company.extension_building_types_hint: Buildings that can be added later through an industry charter.
company.only_used_buildings: Only buildings used by existing companies
company.prestige_goods_hint: Prestige goods the company can produce.
company.modifiers_hint: Effects on the country while the company is prosperous. Percent modifiers are written as fractions: 0.1 means +10%.
company.only_used_modifiers: Only modifiers used by existing companies
company.headquarters_hint: States where the company prefers to set up its headquarters. Choose them on the map; it can mark the headquarters of existing companies.
company.conditions_hint: Add conditions row by row; every row must be met. Anything the rows cannot show stays as a script row.
company.extra_hint: Any other fields of the company, written as they are (for example uses_dynamic_naming or replaces_company).
block.potential: If these are not met, the company is hidden completely. Empty: always shown.
block.attainable: If these are not met, the company is shown only as a potential company.
block.possible: When these are met too, the company can be founded. Empty: always.
block.can_establish_in: States where the company's buildings may be, checked for each state. Empty: anywhere.
block.prestige_goods_trigger: Company scope, written as script. Whether the company can produce its prestige goods.
block.ai_construction_targets: Buildings the AI builds up while working towards the company.
block.ai_weight: How strongly the AI prefers this company over others. The base game uses 3 for flavored companies.
note.no_ai: The AI never founds this company.
note.no_name: No name entered yet: the game will show the key.
problem.key_invalid: The key may only contain letters, digits, _ . and -
problem.key_exists: Another company already uses this key.
problem.buildings_missing: Choose at least one building type.
problem.modifier_value: A bonus value is not a number (or yes / no).
error.offline: The builder is not running. Start app.py again.
error.server_error: Something went wrong in the builder. See the console window for details.
error.not_loaded: The game data is not loaded yet.
error.folders_invalid: The folders are not set correctly.
error.browse_unavailable: The folder dialog could not be opened. Type the path instead.
error.unsupported_texture: This image format cannot be shown.
error.open_folder_failed: Could not open the mod folder.
ai.mode_hint.same: The AI founds the company as soon as it can be founded.
ai.mode_hint.custom: When these are met, the AI picks the company and works towards it. The base game usually asks for less here than to found it.
ai.mode_hint.never: Only players can found this company.
ai.weight_script: This weight is written as a formula; edit it as script.
cond.unreadable: The script has unmatched { }. Fix it below to edit the rows again.
cond.hidden: Hide these conditions in the game (the base game does this when “Can be founded when” already covers them)
template.title: Quick template: company tied to a state region
template.hint: Fills in the conditions and AI the way the base game's flavored companies do. You can still change every row afterwards.
template.confirm: This replaces the current conditions, AI conditions and AI construction targets. Continue?
template.applied: Template applied. Check the rows below.
home.type.factory_hint: Add production buildings with their own production methods, or change existing buildings.
factory.discard_confirm: The factory being edited has unsaved changes. Discard them?
factory.already_in_project: Your mod already changes this building; opened that version.
factory.missing: {key} was not found in the loaded data.
factory.override_note: This changes an existing building from "{source}". The original file is not touched; your mod replaces the whole definition when it loads after it.
factory.key_hint: Internal name used in the files. Letters, digits and _ only, usually starting with building_.
factory.group_hint: Decides what kind of building it is: industry, farm, ranch, plantation or resource extraction.
fset.title: Building settings
fset.hint: Common fields of the building. They are written in the other script below, and the two stay in step. Fields left unset use the game's default.
fset.unreadable: The { } in the other script do not match. Fix it below to use these settings again.
factory.resource_note: Buildings in this group can only be built where the state region lists them (arable_resources / capped_resources). This tool does not change state regions yet, so that needs to be done separately.
factory.city_type_hint: Where the building shows on the map. Filled in from the building group; can be changed.
factory.technologies_hint: Leave empty when it is available from the start.
factory.pmgs_hint: Each group is one slot on the building panel; one of its production methods is active at a time. Use an existing group as it is, or make the factory's own.
factory.pmgs_empty: No groups yet. A factory needs at least one.
factory.copy_own_hint: Makes a copy that belongs to this factory. Other buildings are not affected.
factory.override_direct_hint: Changes the original for every building that uses it.
factory.override_shared:
This is also used by {count} others: {names}.
They will all change. Continue?
factory.pmg_override_note: This overrides the existing group for every building that uses it.
factory.pm_override_note: This overrides the existing production method wherever it is used.
factory.is_default: Default method of the group (otherwise the first one is)
factory.modifiers_hint: Value, what it applies to, and how it scales. Percent modifiers are decimals: 0.1 means +10%.
factory.conditions_hint: Checked for each state. Add conditions one by one; all of them must hold.
factory.ai_value_hint: How much the AI wants this building. Base game factories use 1000.
factory.ai_value_script: This value is written as a formula; edit it as script.
factory.estimate_hint: At base prices, without market price changes. Wages are an estimate: laborers (wage weight 1) earn just enough, after 10% tax, to buy the needs of the chosen standard of living for {people} people (themselves and their dependents); other jobs get their wage weight times that. In the game, each building raises and lowers its wages with its profits.
fblock.potential: Where the building can appear at all. Empty means everywhere.
fblock.possible: Must also hold before it can be built. Empty means always.
fproblem.key_invalid: "{name}": a key may only contain letters, digits, _ . and -
fproblem.key_exists: Another building already uses the key {name}.
fproblem.group_invalid: The building group is not a valid key.
fproblem.city_type_invalid: The city type is not a valid key.
fproblem.construction_invalid: The construction cost must be a number or a known cost.
fproblem.pmgs_missing: Add at least one production method group.
fproblem.pmg_key_missing: A production method group has no key.
fproblem.pmg_key_invalid: Group "{name}": a key may only contain letters, digits, _ . and -
fproblem.pmg_key_exists: The group key {name} is already used.
fproblem.pm_key_missing: A production method has no key.
fproblem.pm_key_invalid: Method "{name}": a key may only contain letters, digits, _ . and -
fproblem.pm_key_exists: The method key {name} is already used.
fproblem.pm_value: Method {name} has an amount or value that is not a number.
fset.label.can_build_government: The state can build it if
fset.label.can_build_private: Private investors can build it if
fset.hint.ownership_type: Production buildings use "can be owned" (self): investors and the state can own it and get its profits.
fset.hint.terrain_manipulator: How the ground around the building looks on the map. Looks only.
fset.hint.levels_per_mesh: One more model on the map every this many levels (default 1). Base game factories use 50.
fset.hint.ai_nationalization_desire: Above 0: the AI prefers to keep it state owned; below 0: it is fine to privatize it.
fset.hint.aliases: Keys the building also answers to, separated by spaces.
fset.hint.can_switch_owner: Unticked, its owner cannot change. The base game does this for subsistence farms, gold mines and the like.
fset.hint.min_raise_to_hire: How much more pay workers need to switch to this building (as a share, 0.3 = 30%).
fset.hint.slaves_role: Which pop type slaves work as here.
fset.hint.economic_contribution: Share of taxes and GDP the building gives, 0 to 1 (default 1).
fset.hint.residence_points_per_level: How much housing each level adds to its city (default 1).
fset.hint.generates_residences: Whether the building adds residences to its city.
fset.hint.category_building_type: Counted as this building in average earnings, productivity and the building list.
fset.hint.valid_pop_culture_traits: Only pops with these culture traits work here.
fset.hint.investment_scores: How investors rate building in each group. Script.
fset.hint.ignore_stateregion_max_level: For groups that cap levels per state region: this building is not capped.
fset.hint.lens: Where it is listed in the build menu, instead of its group's section.
fset.hint.can_build_government: Checked for each state. Empty means always.
fset.hint.can_build_private: Checked for each state. Empty means always.
fset.hint.should_auto_expand: Building scope; replaces the group's rule. Empty means the group's rule.
fset.hint.construction_modifier: Applied to the construction while it is built. Script.
fset.hint.ai_selection: How the AI picks a method of this group (default most_profitable).
fset.hint.is_hidden_when_unavailable: Not shown at all while it cannot be picked.
fset.hint.required_input_goods: These goods must be available to the building to use this method.
fset.hint.unlocking_production_methods: Methods of the same building one of which must be active.
fset.hint.unlocking_global_technologies: Technologies someone in the world must have researched.
fset.hint.unlocking_identity: Power bloc identities, any one of them.
fset.hint.replacement_if_valid: Switched to this method once it can be used.
fset.hint.profession_ratio: Shares of the jobs per pop type.
fset.hint.ai_weight: How much the AI likes this method (default 1).
fset.hint.ai_value: Extra value the AI gives this method.
fset.hint.scoring_override: A special rule the AI uses to pick this method.
fset.hint.pollution_generation: Pollution added to its state region while active (default 0).
fset.hint.city_lights_color_index: Colour of the city lights at night; must match the game's colour list.
fset.hint.timed_modifiers: Modifiers the building gets for a while after switching to this method. Script.
fset.warn.ownership_type: Production buildings use self. Not set or no_ownership: nobody can invest in or own it and its profits go to the state; other: the setting of company headquarters and financial districts that own other buildings.
fset.warn.terrain_manipulator: urban_city and urban_port are the look of city centres and ports only.
fset.warn.buildable: Unticked, players cannot build it; it only comes from history or scripts.
fset.warn.expandable: Unticked, it cannot be expanded and stays at one level.
fset.warn.aliases: Old names of a base game building. A new factory using them clashes with that building; leave empty.
factory.extra_hint: Fields the tool does not know (for example from mods), written as they are. Known fields typed here move to the form above.
factory.pmg_extra_hint: Fields of the group the tool does not know, written as they are.
factory.pm_extra_hint: Fields of the method the tool does not know, written as they are.
image.import_hint: Use a picture of your own (PNG, JPG, WebP… or DDS). It is packed into the mod when you save.
image.fit_contain: Scaled to fit {size}, keeping its shape; the space around it is transparent.
image.fit_cover: Scaled to fill {size}, keeping its shape, and cut to size around the centre.
image.packed_note: Saved as PNG. It goes into the mod's gfx folder when you save; imported pictures nothing uses are removed then.
image.dds_note: DDS files are imported as they are, without resizing (the game uses {size} here). Import it?
error.image_kind: This picture cannot be used here.
error.image_too_large: The picture is too large (20 MB at most).
error.image_format: This file is not a picture that can be read.
home.type.monument_hint: Add monuments and skyscrapers with their map position, model and effects, or change existing ones.
monument.discard_confirm: The monument being edited has unsaved changes. Discard them?
monument.already_in_project: Your mod already changes this monument; opened that version.
monument.location_hint: Choose on the map where it can be built (the state) and where its model stands (the point you click). Without a state it can be built anywhere (still only once), with no model on the map. White marks on the map are existing monuments.
monument.history_hint: Players cannot build it (buildable = no); it stands in the state from the start, owned by the country chosen.
monument.history_no_owner: No country owns this state when the game starts.
monument.models_hint: Pick from the models the loaded buildings use.
monument.effects_hint: A list of effects (one production method, as base game monuments have), or production method groups as for factories.
monument.effects_switch_confirm: Switching clears the effects set so far. Continue?
monument.effects_override: This overrides the monument's own production method.
monument.effects_broken: The effects do not have the shape of a list. Switch to production method groups to edit them.
monument.effects_others: The player can also switch it to: {names} (kept as they are).
monument.note_anywhere: No state: it can be built anywhere, and no model is shown on the map.
monument.note_no_position: No model position: the model will not be shown on the map. Click the map to set it.
fproblem.history_state: A monument that exists at the start needs a state.
fproblem.history_override: An overridden monument cannot be set to exist at the start.
fset.hint.unique: Only one level in the whole world, and private investors never build it.
fset.hint.enable_air_connection: Its region counts for air travel.
fset.hint.statue: The building is a power bloc statue.
fset.hint.entity_constructed: The model shown on the map once it is built.
fset.hint.entity_under_construction: The scaffolding shown while it is built.
fset.hint.entity_not_constructed: Shown before it is built; empty shows nothing.
fset.hint.city_gfx_interactions: How much room it takes in the city picture, and whether other buildings there are cleared.
fset.hint.meshes: Models placed on the terrain. Script.
factory.spending_short: State spending a week (standard of living {level})
factory.estimate_funded_hint: The state funds this building (as monuments and government buildings): it pays the wages and the inputs from its budget, so instead of a profit this shows what the state pays a week (inputs − outputs + wages). In the game, government wages follow the country's normal wage and the government wage setting of the budget.
home.type.law_hint: Change the game's laws or add new laws and law groups: effects, conditions and interest group stances.
law.title: Laws
law.board_hint: As in the game: click a law group to unfold its laws. Click a law to change it; the last line of a group adds a new law to it.
law.changed_hint: Laws of this group your mod changes or adds
law.default_hint: Countries whose history sets no law of this group start with this one.
law.copy_hint: Copy as a new law of this group, with the interest group stances of the copied law
law.discard_confirm: The law being edited has unsaved changes. Discard them?
law.version_confirm: Starting from another version discards your changes. Continue?
law.version_hint: Several sources define this law: pick the version to start from.
law.override_note: This changes an existing law (from {source}). Your mod replaces its whole definition; other content that checks this law keeps working, so changing what it does is safe.
law.key_hint: The name used in files. Letters, digits and _ only; usually starts with law_.
law.group_locked: The law group is set where the law was made and cannot change.
law.progressiveness_hint: How progressive the law is compared with the others of its group (base game: about −100 to 100). Countries with similar laws like each other more.
law.images_hint: Choose from the game's and the loaded mods' law icons, or import your own.
law.stances_hint: Interest groups take their stance on a law from their ideologies. A new law can take the stances of another law of its group (its parent law); the game also treats it as a variant of that law.
law.no_parent: No parent law (every interest group is neutral)
law.parent_hint: Only laws of the same group without a parent law of their own.
law.parent_override_hint: An existing law without a parent law keeps the stances the ideologies give it.
law.stances_note: Added up from the ideologies each interest group starts with; in the game, leaders and events change ideologies.
law.progression: Laws of the group by progressiveness
law.effects_hint: Modifiers the country gets while the law is in effect.
law.institution_hint: The law sets up this institution, which the country can invest in.
law.institution_modifier_hint: Modifiers of the institution, for each level of investment (to be confirmed in the game).
law.special_hint: Taxation laws give modifiers for each tax level; citizenship laws give modifiers for acceptance.
law.list_hint.unlocking_laws: Other laws the country needs (in the base game, the people's army needs a council republic or factory councils).
law.list_hint.requires_law_or: The country needs one of these laws.
law.list_hint.disallowing_laws: The law cannot be enacted while one of these is in effect.
law.block_hint.is_visible: Countries that see the law at all. Empty: every country.
law.block_hint.can_enact: Further conditions to enact the law.
law.block_hint.on_enact: Effects run while the law is being enacted.
law.block_hint.on_activate: Effects run when the law takes effect.
law.block_hint.on_deactivate: Effects run when another law of the group replaces it.
law.block_hint.can_impose: Conditions for an overlord to impose the law on its subject (scope:target_country).
law.block_hint.ai_impose_chance: How much an AI overlord wants to impose the law (a script value).
law.block_hint.ai_will_do: Conditions for the AI to consider the law; empty means always.
law.block_hint.ai_enact_weight_modifier: Added to how much the AI wants to enact the law (base game: +750 while a journal entry asks for it).
law.ai_petitions: Use the base game's petitions weight
law.scripts_hint: Effects written as script. Empty ones are left out.
law.extra_hint: Fields of the law this tool has no form for, as script.
law.note_no_parent: No parent law: every interest group is neutral about this law, so no one pushes for or against it.
lproblem.key_invalid: The key may only contain letters, digits, _, . and -.
lproblem.key_exists: A law with this key already exists.
lproblem.group_unknown: The law group is not in the loaded data.
lproblem.parent: The parent law must be another law of the same group.
lproblem.modifier_value: Modifier values must be numbers (or yes/no).
law.limit_hierarchy_hint: This law group is tied to a social hierarchy (common/social_hierarchies), which only some pops belong to.
law.new_group_neutral: Laws of a new law group have no parent law to take stances from: every interest group is neutral about them.
lgroup.discard_confirm: The law group being edited has unsaved changes. Discard them?
lgroup.delete_confirm: Delete the law group "{name}"? Its {count} laws in your mod are deleted with it.
lgroup.note_no_laws: The group has no laws yet: it needs at least one, which every country starts with.
lgroup.key_hint: The name used in files. Letters, digits and _ only; usually starts with lawgroup_.
lgroup.category_locked: The column the group was made in; it stays.
lgroup.opinion_impact_hint: How much this group's laws count when countries compare how alike their laws are (base game: 0.25 to 2).
lgroup.enactment_days_hint: Days of an enactment cycle before legitimacy counts; empty uses the game's default.
lgroup.approval_mult_hint: How strongly changing a law of this group moves interest group approval; empty is 1.
lgroup.regime_change_hint: As the base game's power structure groups: these laws change with a regime change.
lgroup.hierarchy_hint: Tie the group to a social hierarchy, as the base game's caste system and Edo system.
lgroup.block_hint.enable: Countries that have this law group at all (base game: the navy model needs a coastal state). Empty: every country.
lgroup.block_hint.change_allowed_trigger: When the country may change the law of this group (base game: some subjects may not).
lgroup.laws_hint: No country's history sets a new group, so every country starts with its first law (the default): the first one you made.
lgroup.laws_after_save: Save the group to add laws to it.
lgroup.extra_hint: Fields of the law group this tool has no form for, as script.
gproblem.key_missing: The law group needs a key.
gproblem.key_invalid: The key may only contain letters, digits, _, . and -.
gproblem.key_exists: A law group with this key already exists.
gproblem.category: The category is not one of the game's.
gproblem.opinion_impact: The ideological opinion weight must be a number.
gproblem.enactment_days: Enactment days must be a whole number.
gproblem.approval_mult: The approval effect must be a number.
gproblem.hierarchy: The social hierarchy is not in the loaded data.
home.type.country_hint: Change how countries start: names, colours, starting laws, ruling interest groups, taxes, technology, wealth and literacy.
country.title: Country starts
country.world_hint: The world as the game starts, in the colours of the countries. Click a country on the map or in the list to change how it starts.
country.all_desc: Laws every country starts with. They are set after all the starts, so they replace what each country's history sets, except in the countries you set a law of that group for.
country.not_existing_hint: This country owns no land when the game starts, so it does not exist then (it may be released or formed later).
country.discard_confirm: Discard the unsaved changes to this country's start?
country.delete_confirm: Remove the changes to {name} from the mod? The country then starts as the game has it.
country.names_hint: Leave a name empty to keep the game's. The names are for the language chosen in the corner.
country.name: Name ({language})
country.name_hint: Replaces the game's name of the country.
country.definition_hint: From the definition in effect ({source}). Changing a field writes the whole definition into your mod (REPLACE_OR_CREATE).
country.cultures_hint: Without a state religion, the country takes the religion of the first culture.
country.reset_hint: Back to what the game has
country.laws_hint: The law the country starts with in each law group, and where it comes from. Click a group to choose another law; laws and law groups are made on the law page.
country.laws_all_hint: Choose a law to set it for every country, or leave a group unset so that each country keeps its own.
country.laws_note: Starting laws are set without checking their conditions: laws for some countries only are set too.
country.law_unset_hint: Each country keeps its own law
country.via_hint.explicit: The country's history sets this law (activate_law).
country.via_hint.default: Nothing sets a law of this group, so the game uses the group's first law.
country.via_hint.all: Your mod sets it for every country.
country.via_hint.mine: Your mod sets it for this country.
country.igs_hint: Tick the ruling interest groups; with none ticked, the game picks them. A name replaces the interest group's name in this country, in the language chosen in the corner.
country.party_hint: Only a party that exists at the start can rule.
country.taxed_goods_hint: Goods with a consumption tax at the start.
country.institutions_hint: Institutions that start with investment; the law that sets up an institution must be in effect.
country.technology_hint: The technologies the country starts with: a tier and extra technologies.
country.tier_hint: Tier 1 is the most advanced (Great Britain), tier 7 the least.
country.techs_hint: Researched on top of the tier.
country.population_hint: How rich and literate the country's people start.
country.other_hint: Statements of the country's history the tool has no form for (journal entries, variables, modifiers, companies…). They stay as they are unless you change them here.
country.no_files: None: the tool writes a new file when needed.
country.flag_hint: The flag is shown as the country's colour for now.
country.note_limited: Laws for some countries only are set too: {names}
country.note_all: These laws replace each country's own, except in the countries you set a law of that group for.
country.note_capital: The capital is not a state the country owns at the start.
country.note_named_from_capital: The game names this country after its capital, so its own name may not show.
cproblem.election: The next election is not a date (year.month.day).
cproblem.cultures: A country needs at least one primary culture.
cproblem.country_unknown: The loaded game data has no such country.
cproblem.law: A starting law is not in the game data, or not in its group.
cproblem.capital: The capital is not a known state.
cproblem.goods: A taxed good is not in the game data.
cproblem.tariffs: A tariff has unknown goods or level.
cproblem.institutions: An institution is unknown or its level is not 1–5.
cproblem.techs: A technology is not in the game data.
cproblem.igs: An interest group is not in the game data.
country.ruling_game: Not set: the game picks them
country.government_hint: The country starts with elections: one of its starting laws gives votes.
country.no_elections: The country starts without elections: none of its starting laws gives votes (distribution of power: {law}). So it has no election date and no ruling party.
country.no_elections_set: Your mod still sets an election date or a ruling party; without elections they do nothing.
country.tariffs_hint: Tariffs or subsidies on the import or export of goods at the start.
country.capital_hint: The capital state. On the map the country's own land is in its colour, other countries are dimmed, and the capital is gold; its own states are listed first.
cproblem.provinces: A province is not on the loaded map.
cproblem.states: A state is not in the loaded data.
cproblem.pops: A pop has an unknown culture, religion or pop type.
cproblem.buildings: A building, its holder or its production method is not in the loaded data.
territory.title: Territory
territory.hint: The country's land is in its colour, other countries are dimmed, its claims are striped and the capital is gold. Pops and buildings go along with the land (see the pops and buildings tabs).
territory.mode_hint.province: Click a province to take it, or one of the country's to give it up (nobody owns it then).
territory.mode_hint.state: Click a state to take all of it, or give it all up when the country has all of it.
territory.mode_hint.claim: Click a state to claim it, or to drop the claim.
territory.parts_hint: The country has a part of {count} states. A part taken whole brings its pops and buildings; a part taken in pieces shares its pops out by provinces and leaves its buildings.
territory.unincorporated_hint: An unincorporated state, as the game's colonies.
territory.release_hint: Give up all the country's provinces of this state: nobody owns them then.
territory.claims_hint: States the country claims at the start. Choose them here or with the claim mode of the map.
territory.note_vanished: These countries are left without land and do not exist at the start: {names}. Their diplomacy and treaties are dropped.
territory.moved_hint: The land changed owners, so this changed with it.
territory.own_reset_hint: Back to what the part gets from the game and the land
territory.pops_hint: The pops of each of the country's parts. Once changed, the list of a part is kept as it is; if the part changes owners again, it starts from the game's again.
territory.buildings_hint: The buildings of each of the country's parts, with who holds their levels and their production methods.
territory.level_hint: Levels nobody holds (as the game's monuments).
mappicker.hint.states: Click states on the map, or search for one.
mappicker.hint.regions: Click the map to choose the whole strategic region, or search for one.
mappicker.no_point: No position on the map yet: click the map in this state.
mappicker.click.states: Click a state to choose it; drag to move, scroll to zoom.
mappicker.click.regions: Click a state to choose its whole strategic region; drag to move, scroll to zoom.
mappicker.click.geographic_regions: Click a state to list the geographic regions it is in; choose them in the list.
mappicker.click.position: Click the map: the state is where it can be built, the point is where its model stands.
cproblem.diplomacy: A diplomatic relation names a country or pact type that is not in the loaded game data.
cproblem.treaty_date: A new treaty's date is not a date (year.month.day).
cproblem.treaty_country: A new treaty is with a country that is not in the loaded game data.
cproblem.treaty_articles: A new treaty needs at least one article, and each one-way article must go from one side to the other.
cproblem.treaty_inputs: An article of a new treaty is missing what it needs (goods, amount, state…), or names something unknown.
cproblem.character_template: A character template is not in the loaded game data.
cproblem.character_name: A new character needs a first and a last name.
cproblem.character_birth: A new character's birth date is not a date (year.month.day).
cproblem.character_fields: A new character needs a culture (and an interest group when it leads one), and what it names must be in the loaded game data.
cproblem.characters: A character has neither a template nor script.
relations.vanished_hint: This country has no land at the start (see the territory tab), so what names it is not written.
relations.role.subject: Overlord:
relations.role_hint.overlord: This country is the overlord; the other country is its subject.
relations.role_hint.subject: This country is the subject of the other country.
relations.role_hint.actor: This country has the pact with the other country (for example its rival or embargo).
relations.role_hint.target: The other country has the pact with this country.
relations.kind_hint.pact: Subject relationships (puppet, colony, personal union…) and other pacts such as rivalries and embargoes.
relations.kind_hint.relations: Starting relations between the two countries, -100 to 100; the game sets them for both.
relations.kind_hint.truce: A truce between the two countries for the given months.
relations.kind_hint.obligation: A favour one country owes the other.
relations.kind_hint.liberty_desire: Added to this country's liberty desire as a subject (-100 to 100); leave it empty for none.
relations.diplomacy_hint: Everything in the diplomacy files this country is part of, on either side. Once you change something, the whole list is written as you see it, and the same statements in other countries' blocks go.
relations.kept_note: Statements the tool does not read (for example inside every_subject_or_below or if) stay as they are.
relations.treaties_hint: The treaties this country is part of. The game's treaties can be removed; new ones can be added. To change one, remove it and add a new one.
relations.dlc_hint: The game writes this treaty twice, with and without a DLC. Removing it removes both.
relations.remove_hint: Take this treaty out of the start
relations.characters_hint: The characters the country starts with. Choose game templates or make new characters; new ones are written as templates of your mod.
relations.many_rulers: {count} characters are rulers; the country has one ruler.
relations.other_characters: {count} other statements of the character history (for example characters inside a condition) stay as they are.
country.new_hint: Make a country of your own: copy a country's settings, or start blank.
country.new_needs_land: The country does not exist at the start until it has land: give it provinces on the territory tab.
country.new_copy_hint: Takes the definition (type, tier, cultures, religion, social hierarchy), the politics (laws, ruling interest groups, taxes, tariffs, institutions, taxed goods), the technology, wealth and literacy. Land, pops, buildings, characters and diplomacy stay with that country.
country.new_blank_hint: A recognized principality; everything else as the game has it (the default law of each group). Choose the cultures and the capital yourself.
country.new_pick_source: Choose the country to copy from.
country.code_hint: Three capital letters or digits, starting with a letter, not used by another country (for example NEW). It cannot be changed later.
country.code_taken: This tag is already used by a country of the game or of your mod.
country.definition_new_hint: The country's definition, written as a new country of your mod.
country.flag_new_hint: A pattern in up to three colours, with emblems on it: single-colour emblems of the game, the game's pictures, or a picture of your own. The game draws it on its own; check it in the game.
cproblem.name_missing: A new country needs a name.
cproblem.color_missing: A new country needs a colour.
cproblem.key_exists: This tag is already used by another country.
cproblem.flag: The flag uses a pattern, emblem or colour that is not in the loaded game data.
flag.order_hint: Position and size are parts of the flag (0.5 is the middle, 1 is the whole width or height). Emblems are drawn under pictures, each in the order of the list.
flag.import_hint: A picture of your own, fitted into the flag's 768×512 with the rest transparent; it covers the whole flag.
country.names_new_hint: The country's names in the language chosen at the top; the game uses English where a language has none.
cproblem.capital_missing: A new country needs a capital.
home.type.goods_hint: Add goods and prestige goods or change existing ones: price, market, pop needs and colour.
goods.title: Goods
goods.board_hint: As in the game's market: click a good for its prestige goods and to change it; drag a good to another column to change its category. The last line of a column adds a new good to it.
goods.pool_hint: Goods no pop need buys. Drag one into a need to add it there (weight 1); drag a good of a need here to take it out of that need.
goods.pending: {count} goods changed on the board are not saved yet.
goods.discard_pending: Discard the changes of {count} goods made on the board?
goods.typed_invalid: Some values typed on the board are wrong (red); fix them to save.
goods.default_stays: {good} is the default good of {need} and stays in it; hold Ctrl while dragging to copy it to another need.
goods.board_hint_needs: Each pop need with the goods that fill it. Drag a good to another need to move it there (hold Ctrl to copy), or to the right to take it out of its need; type its weight (above 0) and max and min shares (0 to 1, min not above max) on its card. ★ marks the need's default good, which stays in its need. The changes are kept until you save them.
goods.prestige_changed_hint: Prestige goods of it your mod adds or changes
goods.copy_hint: A new good with the same settings
goods.discard_confirm: The good has unsaved changes. Discard them?
goods.delete_prestige: Its {count} prestige goods in your mod are deleted with it.
goods.delete_used: {count} buildings of your mod still make or use it; their production methods will name a good that is gone.
goods.no_needs: Not in any pop need: pops do not buy it.
goods.note_no_producer: No building makes it yet: add it to the outputs of a production method on the factory page.
goods.note_no_buyer: Nobody buys it yet: add it to a pop need, or to the inputs of a production method.
goods.note_rewrite: These needs are written again in whole: {needs}
goods.no_color: No colour set: the game picks one.
goods.save_first: Shown once the good is saved and used in production methods.
goods.override_note: This changes the game's good (from {source}). Only what you change is written: the definition, its colour, its entries in the pop needs.
goods.key_hint: Lowercase letters, digits and _; the key is also the name of its icon in texts (@key!).
goods.category_hint: The column of the market screen it is listed in.
goods.cost_hint: Price at balanced supply and demand; the base game uses 20 to 100.
goods.flag.tradeable: Can be traded on the world market
goods.flag.local: Local: only used in the state it is made in
goods.flag_hint.tradeable: Off for goods such as gold.
goods.flag_hint.fixed_price: The price does not follow supply and demand (gold).
goods.flag_hint.pop_consumption_can_add_: As automobiles in the base game.
goods.number_hint.traded_quantity: How much one world market trade moves; also the convoy cost of goods transfer treaties. Empty: 10.
goods.number_hint.convoy_cost_multiplier: Convoy cost when it is shipped as military supply. Empty: 1.
goods.number_hint.obsession_chance: Relative chance that pops become obsessed with it; empty or 0: never.
goods.number_hint.consumption_tax_cost: Authority it costs to tax its consumption; empty: it cannot be taxed.
goods.needs_hint: Pops buy a good to fill their needs. In a need, the goods share the demand by their weight; the supply shares cap and floor how much of it one good gets.
goods.rewrite_warn: You changed or removed entries the game has, so these needs are written again in whole: {needs}. Later updates of mods loaded before yours that change them do not come through.
goods.number_hint.prestige_factor: Prestige for the lowest awarded place of its production ranking, doubled for every place above. Empty: none.
goods.color_failed: The icon could not be read.
goods.color_hint: Its colour in the market charts.
goods.texticon_hint: The text icon @{key}! is made from the icon, for the texts of its modifiers.
goods.texticon_game: The game's text icon is kept.
goods.extra_hint: Fields this tool has no form for, kept as they are.
pgood.copy_hint: A new prestige good with the same settings
pgood.discard_confirm: The prestige good has unsaved changes. Discard them?
pgood.note_no_company: No company can make it yet: add it to a company's prestige goods on the company page.
pgood.key_hint: The base game starts these keys with prestige_good_.
pgood.base_locked: The good it was made under on the board.
pgood.bonus_hint: The base game uses 0.1 for every prestige good.
pgood.possible_hint: The base game asks only for the Charters of Commerce DLC.
pgood.companies_hint: Which companies can make it is set on the company page, in each company's prestige goods.
gdproblem.key_invalid: The key may only have letters, digits, _ . and -.
gdproblem.key_exists: A good with this key already exists.
gdproblem.cost: The base price must be a number above 0.
gdproblem.number: A number field has something that is not a number.
gdproblem.need: A pop need is unknown or listed twice.
gdproblem.need_value: A value in the pop needs is not a number.
gdproblem.need_weight: The weight in a need must be a number above 0.
gdproblem.need_share: The max and min shares must be numbers from 0 to 1.
gdproblem.need_order: The min share cannot be above the max share.
pgproblem.key_missing: The prestige good needs a key.
pgproblem.key_invalid: The key may only have letters, digits, _ . and -.
pgproblem.key_exists: A prestige good with this key already exists.
pgproblem.base_good: The base good does not exist.
pgproblem.icon_missing: The prestige good needs an icon.
pgproblem.prestige_bonus: The prestige bonus must be a number.
goods.version_hint: Several sources define it: choose the version to start from.
